title: My device was leaked by Suno
description: Suno, an AI music generator, experienced a limited security incident in late 2025 that was publicly disclosed in mid-2026. The breach involved outdated source code that is no longer in use, and the company confirmed no sensitive personal information was compromised. The incident revealed that Suno trained its AI model by scraping millions of songs and lyrics from platforms including YouTube, Deezer, and Genius. Suno is currently facing copyright infringement lawsuits from major music labels. The hacker claimed no specific motivation beyond general interest in hacking. Users are advised to be cautious if they have Suno accounts.

aiSummary: In late 2025, Suno was subject to a limited security incident involving outdated source code, which was quickly contained and investigated. No sensitive personal data, including full credit card numbers, was compromised according to the vendor. The breach exposed that Suno's AI music generator trained its models using data scraped from multiple music platforms such as YouTube, Deezer, and Genius. The incident was publicly reported in 2026. Suno is currently involved in legal disputes over copyright infringement related to its AI training methods. The hacker responsible stated no targeted motivation.
aiImpact: The breach did not compromise sensitive personal information or full credit card data. However, it exposed Suno's use of scraped music and lyrics from various platforms to train its AI models, which has legal and reputational implications. The incident contributes to ongoing copyright infringement lawsuits against Suno by major music labels. Users with Suno accounts should remain vigilant, but there is no evidence of direct personal data theft or financial fraud from this incident.
